Key points
• The major energy supplying fuels in the body are glucose, lactate, fatty acids, ketone bodies, some amino acids and ethanol,
with minor contributions from fructose, galactose, glycerol and limited amounts from short chain fatty acids produced by
the colonic microbiota.
• During metabolism the energy in the fuels is converted by speciﬁc pathways to a number of end products but the useable
energy is conserved in reducing equivalents (NADH and FADH2) and primarily acetyl CoA.
• The only anaerobic pathway of energy metabolism is glycolysis, the breakdown of glucose (and other sugars) to lactate
